subject: Private control-plane: network & identity handoff for Acme on-prem deployment

Subject: Private control-plane: network & identity handoff for Acme on-prem deployment

Hi Raj —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for your private control-plane deployment. Per our kickoff, this thread is to align on the identity and network handoff so your security team can sign off and we can proceed with the on-prem connector cutover. High level approach we recommend:

- SAML SSO (IdP-initiated + SP-initiated) for human users. We rely on signed SAML assertions and recommend including NameID and an attribute for email and user_role.
- SCIM 2.0 push for automated user/group provisioning. Preferred flow: push from Acme IdP to Redwood SCIM endpoint (HTTPS, mutual TLS optional).
- Service accounts / cross-account IAM roles for machine-to-machine (on-prem infra -> Redwood control-plane). We provide role templates that map to least-privilege scopes (reporting, deploy, admin).
- Network considerations: control-plane endpoints are reachable over TLS; if you are air-gapped, we can support a relay (bastion/proxy) inside your VPC that forwards SAML/SCIM traffic to our private control-plane endpoint.

Immediate asks for your side so we can generate the runbook:
1) IdP metadata XML (SAML) + contact for SSO admin
2) SCIM test account (or a webhook URL) for initial provisioning test
3) IP ranges to allow in your egress/NAT (we will share ours once we have your network model)
4) Desired role names and a small mapping of current AD/Okta groups to Redwood roles (CSV is fine)

Attaching: redwood-scim-sample-mappings.xlsx (sample mappings and attribute expectations).

If this aligns, can we target a validation window the week of Jan 22? I’ll schedule 60 minutes for a live validation with your infra and security teams.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

David —

Appreciate the clear checklist. Some clarifications from our side after an internal sync with security and platform:

- Security prefers SCIM push-only (no pull) and requires provisioning calls be from our internal egress IPs and use TLS 1.2+ with server cert validation. Is mutual TLS required on your end or optional?
- We will sign SAML assertions using our company key. Our SSO team would like to verify the expected assertion claims. Can you confirm the exact attribute names Redwood expects (email, name, groups, user_role)?
- On-prem deployments: we cannot allow outbound to arbitrary public IPs from the control-plane network. Would a proxy inside our edge DMZ that forwards to Redwood be acceptable, provided the connection is only to specific FQDNs and ports?
- For machine identities, we prefer using short-lived tokens derived from a signed JWT from our token server. Can you support role assumption using JWT assertions rather than long-term static keys?

We attached a preliminary IdP metadata file and our network diagram (ops team). We also want to loop in IdCloud (our integration partner) to discuss a connector they offer — cc'd.

Questions for Redwood to answer before our validation window:
- Confirm SCIM endpoints and an example provisioning request/response
- Provide the role templates you mentioned (least-privilege examples) and how they map to SCIM groups
- Documented cert rotation cadence for SAML signing keys and for any mTLS certs used in the connector

Thanks,
Raj
Raj Patel
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

Raj / team —

Quick responses from Redwood security/architecture standpoint:

- Mutual TLS for SCIM is optional; we support both bearer token (TLS + OAuth) and MTLS. For highly regulated customers we recommend mTLS (client certs issued by customer CA or via our CA onboarding).
- Assertion attributes: we expect (case-sensitive) attributes: email, fullName, groups (array) and role_hint (if you have a direct role mapping). We will accept groups as either a CSV within an attribute or as multiple group attributes depending on IdP. We included a short attribute mapping table in our private playbook (link below).
- Proxy model: acceptable. If traffic will traverse a proxy/bastion, we need the TLS termination to be end-to-end to Redwood (no TLS termination in an untrusted hop). In practice customers keep a TCP-level forwarder that preserves TLS. Please ensure SNI/FQDN passthrough so our cert validation works.
- Machine auth: we support JWT-based role assertions (OIDC JWT with aud claim pointing to our control-plane) and short-lived tokens minted by Redwood after assertion validation. This avoids sharing static long-term keys.

Operational requirements we will validate in the runbook:
1) IdP metadata + test SAML user details
2) SCIM test client (or OAuth client creds) and an endpoint for push tests
3) List of SSO admins who should receive emergency-recovery access and the offboarding procedure
4) Network egress rules + proxy details (IP/FQDN, port 443, any TLS inspection notes)
5) Audit/logging: we will publish audit events to the private control-plane logs; you can pull via our secure log-forwarder or we can push a subset as JSON to your SIEM endpoint (TLS + token)

Security notes:
- Ensure your IdP rotation policy is documented; Redwood will re-import metadata on rotation if you notify us or we can rotate on a schedule.
- For SCIM, prefer group-scoped mapping so removing a user from groups triggers deprovisioning.
- For emergency access, Redwood supports a time-bound admin elevation flow with multi-approval if you require it.

I'll join the Jan 22 validation session if that works; Priyom, can you prepare the role templates and a draft SCIM-to-role mapping before then? Marissa, please add the playbook link to the meeting invite.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
